Assign a soil depth in centimeters to every pixel

Source: R/CreateDepthmap3.R
create_depthmap.Rd

Builds a per-pixel depth map from the imaging geometry. geometry selects the shape being imaged, and the shape decides which of the two corrections apply: foreshortening of the depth axis by the insertion angle, and the depth spread across a curved surface.

Usage

create_depthmap(
  img,
  mask = NULL,
  sinoid = TRUE,
  tube_thicc = 7,
  tilt = NULL,
  dpi = 300,
  start_soil = 0,
  center_offset = 0.5,
  geometry = NULL,
  angle_from_vertical = 45
)

Arguments

img

Input image (accepts terra SpatRaster, matrix, array, or file path). For multi-band images, specify band_index parameter

mask

Raster mask indicating foreign objects (1 = mask, 0 or NA = keep)

sinoid

Logical. Superseded by geometry, and kept so existing code runs unchanged: TRUE means geometry = "tube", FALSE means geometry = "window". Ignored when geometry is given.

tube_thicc

Numeric; diameter of minirhizotron tube in cm. Used by geometry = "tube" only

tilt

Numeric. Superseded by angle_from_vertical, which states the convention in its name. Degrees from horizontal, the opposite reference, so tilt = t is angle_from_vertical = 90 - t. Given it, the conversion is applied and a warning says so. 45 is the same angle either way

dpi

Numeric; image resolution in dots per inch

start_soil

Numeric; soil surface boundary in cm (0 = surface)

center_offset

Numeric in [0, 1]; where the top of the tube – the shallowest line of the curvature wave – sits across the image height, as a fraction of one full tube circumference. 0 puts it on the first row, 0.5 halfway down, 1 on the last row. 0 and 1 are the same point on the tube, the image seam. Used by geometry = "tube" only

geometry

Character; the shape being imaged. One of "tube" (default), "window" or "flat" – see Geometries.

angle_from_vertical

Numeric; insertion angle in degrees measured from vertical, in [0, 90]. 0 is an upright tube and 90 a horizontal one, so the number is how far the tube leans over – the convention field notes usually record ("installed at 45 degrees"). Used by geometry = "tube" and "window".

The angle splits a tube's depth between its two axes, and the two terms are complements. The depth gained along the tube's length scales by cos(angle_from_vertical): an upright tube gains a full centimeter of depth per centimeter of tube, a horizontal one gains none. The depth spread around its circumference scales by sin(angle_from_vertical): an upright tube's cross-section is horizontal, so its whole circumference sits at one depth, while a horizontal tube's upper side is a full diameter above its lower side.

Value

terra raster object containing the depth map

Geometries

"tube"

A cylindrical minirhizotron tube, unrolled by the scanner. Depth increases along the image width and is scaled by cos(angle_from_vertical); a curvature wave spanning one circumference is added across the image height, scaled by sin(angle_from_vertical). Needs tube_thicc, angle_from_vertical and center_offset.

"window"

A planar rhizotron window. Depth increases along the image width and is scaled by cos(angle_from_vertical), with no curvature term. tube_thicc and center_offset are unused.

"flat"

A surface with no depth axis at all – a flatbed scan of washed roots on a tray. Every pixel is at the same depth, -start_soil, so a profile over this map collapses to one depth bin. tube_thicc, angle_from_vertical and center_offset are unused.

Author

Johannes Cunow, Robert Weigel

Examples

data(seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067)
seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067 = terra::rast(seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067)
img = seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067
mask = seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067[[1]] - seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067[[2]]
mask[mask == 255] <- NA
map = create_depthmap(img, mask, start_soil = 0.1,
  geometry = "tube",
  tube_thicc = 7,
  angle_from_vertical = 45,
  dpi = 300,
  center_offset = 0.1 )

# A tray of washed roots: no depth axis, so every pixel gets one depth
flat = create_depthmap(img, geometry = "flat", dpi = 300)
terra::minmax(flat)
#>     lyr.1
#> min     0
#> max     0
